reason: Both kill the 2/1 Cleric; Theorix Charm is the right-sized answer, saving Bitter Triumph (and 3 life or a card) for Amalia/Haliya, and Verge gives colored mana.
Ingris uses all three mana while the opponent has only 1 open (no Countersculpt), developing an evasive threat; B wastes mana on a 2-drop with no trigger.
Uses all mana; an extra equipment survives sweepers, carries hone counters and counts toward Kili's storied; little downside against a control deck.
Voice of Victory stops flashing it on the opponent's turn, so holding Enduring Curiosity wastes it; cast it now as a blocker and card engine against an opponent at 7.
Flashing in Drowner with no target throws away its stun/shuffle removal, which matters a lot against equipped Dwarves; a 2/1 body is minor.
Triple-blocking kills Haliya and blocks more attackers, so you take less damage at 6 life; B only chumps and takes more damage.
A two-lander on the play in a 20-land deck full of cheap spells, with removal that lines up well against early landfall creatures; worth keeping.
Evoking Deceit to bounce a 1/1 or Relic is a poor 2-for-1 against aggro; Winternight Stories digs for lands and threats at full value.
Killing a Vinelasher now or later in the turn plays out about the same; waiting only adds a little information.
Next turn, Leyline Axe on the 5/4 token plus Mauler is about lethal from 15; Jace can bounce the Axe or make a chump blocker and draw damage, while holding counters can't stop an equip.
